requirements.facts: AB is a short upright object at far left. A1B1 is a larger inverted intermediate real image between objective and eyepiece; A1 is below the shared axis and B1 lies on it. A2 is above the axis on the rear retina, with B2 on the axis. A, B, A1, B1, A2, B2 are all source labels.

The objective is the first vertical double-ended outward-arrow lens symbol, near x194. Two hollow focus markers lie on the shared axis near x84 and x311. A horizontal F1 bracket above joins the objective plane to the right focus plane, with vertical extension from the right focus. No numerical focal length is given.

The second vertical double-ended outward-arrow lens symbol is near x658. B1 is at the left focal plane of the eyepiece; the vertical extension through B1 joins the F2 bracket above to the eyepiece plane. The source F2 bracket is horizontal; no numerical focal length is given.

Two solid, forward-directed rays leave A, refract at the objective, cross at A1, continue to the eyepiece, emerge as approximately parallel rays, enter the eye, and converge at A2. The eye is a single closed schematic outline with an anterior opening/lens region and posterior retinal image. The scanned sketch is approximate, not a scale drawing.

There are no source dashed answer extensions. The shared principal axis, rays, object/image strokes, lens symbols, eye contour, F1/F2 brackets and extensions are solid. Any dashed eye-lens plane in the modern schematic is an explicitly declared modern guide, not a source ray.

modernAdditionsOrRegularization: Level the slightly scan-tilted principal axis and make both lens planes vertical.
Use an internally coherent approximate paraxial schematic; source distances and apparent image magnifications are not numerical givens.
English Objective, Eyepiece, Eye lens and Retina labels identify the schematic apparatus; they are modern additions.
A muted dashed eye-lens plane identifies the refraction plane. It is not an extension ray, an inferred exercise answer or source dashed content.
Normalize mathematical subscripts to ASCII A1/B1/A2/B2/F1/F2 labels.

requirements.facts: One solid horizontal principal-axis segment MN, M at the left and N at the right. S is an eight-spoke luminous-point mark above the axis, toward the left. S1 is a small hollow point below the axis, toward the right. Horizontal order M < S < S1 < N; S is farther above the axis than S1 is below it. No ray, lens plane, optical center or focus is drawn.

modernAdditionsOrRegularization: Level the two-pixel scan tilt of MN using its mean source y149; preserve source x coordinates and vertical offsets with one uniform scale.
Small endpoint anchors for M and N do not identify a lens center.
Keep S1 as an ASCII mathematical label; star spokes are marker strokes only, not answer rays.

requirements.facts: One solid horizontal principal-axis segment MN, with M left and N right. A and B are small hollow point marks above the axis. A is toward the upper left; B is lower and farther right. Horizontal order M < A < B < N and vertical order A > B > MN. No connecting line AB, construction ray, lens plane, optical center or focus is present. The same unassigned A/B figure serves both source-to-image directions in exercise8.
